claims.text: AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles synthesized by pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane are initially sub-5 nm and elliptical.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles possess a metastable FCC structure governed by kinetic effects rather than thermodynamic entropy stabilization.
Surface-energy gradients override sluggish diffusion in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Au and Cu have sufficiently low cohesive energies to drive their surface segregation and evaporation in this alloy.
Rapid Au and Cu surface segregation and evaporation become dominant above approximately 800 K.
The segregation and evaporation rate is highly sensitive to whether the initial particle is icosahedral or a truncated octahedron.
Shape sensitivity arises from differences in surface-atom coordination and curvature.
Local curvature-induced chemical-potential differences lower the activation energy for Au and Cu surface diffusion relative to bulk diffusion.
The high surface-to-volume ratio of sub-5 nm particles amplifies the thermodynamic driving force for Au and Cu surface segregation.
Au and Cu are the low-surface-energy elements in the AuCoCuNiPt system.
Surface diffusion is activated by the high surface energy of the FCC lattice and by shape-specific coordination environments such as high-index facets.
Greater grain-boundary or defect density is associated with higher surface free energy.
Elevated-temperature treatment can produce element-selective near-surface enrichment and depletion in a high-entropy alloy.
Au and Cu evaporate after surface enrichment because their cohesive energies are lower than those of Pt, Ni, and Co.
Heating causes progressive Au and Cu loss and widens the nanoparticle size distribution.
Heating transforms elliptical nanoparticles into spherical particles through surface-energy minimization.
Selective Au and Cu loss produces a core-shell structure enriched in Pt, Ni, and Co.
Transformation is significantly faster for elliptical particles than for truncated octahedrons because elliptical particles have greater curvature and defect density.
Surface-energy control is dominant only below 10 nm.
For bulk alloys or particles larger than 20 nm, surface-energy-driven segregation is suppressed and sluggish bulk diffusion remains rate limiting.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and uncertainty frame the relevant shape comparison as icosahedral versus truncated octahedral, whereas the conditions and proposed experiment compare elliptical versus truncated-octahedral particles. Thus the stated boundary condition is not the one directly tested.
